verdict.rationale: Greptile documents a learning system that trains on team emoji reactions and explanatory replies, so it stops commenting on things the team doesn't care about after 2-3 weeks. It also captures conventions as coding patterns you can create and search via MCP, indexes existing rule files like CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and lets you scope rules and context per directory. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the learned memory persists and changes future reviews, and detail on how past review decisions are stored, viewed or edited as memory.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the reviewer builds a persistent memory of my team's conventions and past review decisions and applies it to future PRs

citations.quote: Your 👍/👎 reactions and replies teach Greptile what matters. After 2-3 weeks, it stops commenting on things you don't care about.
Greptile learns from your team's feedback to provide increasingly relevant suggestions. The primary training methods are emoji reactions and explanatory comments.
With MCP, you can view, search, and create patterns from your IDE.
Automatically index existing rule files like Claude.md, AGENTS.md, and cursor.rules for richer review context.
Scope review settings, rules, and context to the directories each team owns.
